PullRequest.Title: chat input: fix padding and jump when attaching
PullRequest.Body:

fixes input jumping when attaching and better collapse behavior

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop new-session composer: add/remove or wrap attachment pills, and resize the Sessions view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Attachment-row size changes are delivered by one ResizeObserver callback that measures the single row and updates the composer's top offset before paint. Outer view resizing synchronously calls NewChatView.doLayout -> NewChatWidget.layout -> NewChatInputWidget.layout; the new offset read occurs before the already-existing editor and two responsive-picker layout passes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One observed attachment row per mounted composer. Attachment count can increase row height through wrapping, but measurement cardinality remains one per observer delivery or outer layout pass rather than one per attachment.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ResizeObserver delivery is serialized by the browser; workbench grid layout and editor/picker layout execute synchronously on the UI thread. No concurrent fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. The row height is re-read on observer delivery and outer layout; warm and cold behavior are equivalent. The observer coalesces DOM size changes according to browser resize-observation delivery.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path, one-row cardinality, disposal, and synchronous DOM measurement; low confidence that the added read creates an additional material layout cycle rather than joining the existing layout flush.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact resize frequency and browser layout cost vary with platform and composer complexity. The added geometry read is real, but surrounding pre-existing editor and responsive-picker layout already performs synchronous geometry reads on the same pass, so an independently material regression is not established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The observer and observed target are disposed with the widget, work is bounded to one row, and the diff does not prove materially worse UI-thread scaling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Phone composer with attachments across viewport-class changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: NewChatInputWidget.layout synchronously checks the main-container phone-layout class and removes the desktop top offset; attachment ResizeObserver callbacks perform the same check. This is UI-thread work before editor and picker layout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One class lookup and at most one inline-style removal per composer layout/observer callback, independent of attachment count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous and serialized on the UI thread; one observer per mounted composer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache. Phone state is read directly from the authoritative main-container class so rotation/breakpoint changes are reflected immediately.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the path is bounded and introduces no fan-out or retained growth.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Viewport rotation and breakpoint crossing are infrequent, and the constant DOM work is too small to establish user-visible degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding; the phone guard prevents desktop offset behavior and adds only constant work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and update new-session status toolbar actions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each rendered MenuItemAction uses NewChatInputStatusActionViewItem. Rendering or an action class update scans the label's small class list, toggles one container class, and for codicons traverses that action item's shallow DOM to substitute a registered compact icon class.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scales with the number of visible status menu actions and their class-update events. Each traversal is confined to one action-item subtree; realistic toolbars contain a small number of actions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Menu rendering and action updates are synchronous and serialized on the UI thread; no async burst or queue is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The selected compact codicon class is retained only on its owning view item so it can be removed before a class refresh. It is lifecycle-bounded by toolbar/view-item disposal; no global or unbounded cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in per-action cardinality and bounded ownership; no evidence of hot-frame invocation or substantial DOM traversal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extensions can contribute additional status actions, but each action adds a tiny bounded subtree/class scan and updates occur only when the action presentation changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The broader provider performs bounded presentation work and does not introduce retained growth or meaningful render-path scaling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Responsive model/session picker compaction during narrow-window resizing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing ChatInputPickerResponsiveLayout performs the synchronous fit/measurement algorithm on resize and mutation. The diff changes compact widths, CSS alignment, and identifies the model picker from its rendered element class; it does not add a new layout loop or expensive boundary.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scales with the existing small number of picker actions in each primary/secondary toolbar. Effective cardinality and observer count are unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Two existing responsive layout controllers run synchronously for primary and secondary lanes; browser observers serialize callbacks. No new concurrency or fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache. Compact state remains in the existing observable and DOM classes, updated by the same responsive layout lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed call sites and responsive-layout implementation that the algorithmic behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The pre-existing responsive algorithm performs substantial DOM measurement, but this diff does not increase its invocation count or item cardinality in production.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding because the PR changes dimensions/presentation without introducing or materially amplifying the existing measurement mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 18 changed files and every diff hunk. Traced desktop/mobile attachment layout, status-action rendering, responsive picker compaction, observer cleanup, and all changed/transitive expensive boundaries. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or concrete regression fix was established.
